metaTitle: Learn Math by Doing the Work | Lune Synth
metaDescription: Lune Synth grades handwritten math, finds the exact step that broke down, and builds targeted practice without doing the thinking for you.
headline: Learn math by doing the work—not watching AI do it.
heroBody: Write the solution on paper. Lune Synth reads your steps, identifies the precise mistake, and turns it into focused practice that helps the next problem feel easier.
phoneAlt: Lune Synth displaying an advanced calculus derivative problem
problemHeadline: Understanding a solution is not the same as building one.
problemBody: A polished answer can feel obvious after someone else has done the hard part. Math sticks when you choose a method, commit the steps to paper, find the break, and repair it yourself. Lune Synth keeps that productive struggle intact while making sure you are never stuck without direction.
contrastBefore: Ask AI for the finished solution
contrastAfter: Submit your work and fix the exact step

benefits.title: Do the work
benefits.body: Solve by hand so every substitution, sign, diagram, and decision stays visible.

benefits.title: Get precise feedback
benefits.body: See where your reasoning changed direction without replacing your solution with ours.

benefits.title: Practice what is weak
benefits.body: Turn one mistake into a short mission aimed at the skill that actually needs repetition.

exampleKicker: One attempt. One useful next step.
exampleHeadline: Feedback that stays inside your solution.
attempt: Correct product-rule setup, then the derivative of ln(x) is written as x instead of 1/x.
observation: Your structure is right. Recheck only the derivative of ln(x) on line three.
hint: What function multiplied by x gives 1? Repair that term and simplify again.
nextPractice: Next mission: logarithmic derivatives with the product rule.
closingHeadline: Make every page of math count.
closingBody: Join the beta and turn handwritten attempts into precise feedback, stronger habits, and practice built around what you actually need next.
clarifier: Join for early access to Lune Synth.

metaTitle: SAT Prep That Makes You Think | Lune Synth
metaDescription: Prepare for SAT Math with handwritten attempts, precise feedback, and targeted practice instead of passive answer review.
headline: Prepare for the SAT by doing the thinking yourself.
heroBody: Work each problem on paper, get feedback on the exact step that cost you the answer, and practice that skill again before test day.
phoneAlt: Lune Synth displaying an SAT algebra practice question
problemKicker: Practice scores hide the real gap
problemHeadline: A wrong answer tells you almost nothing about what went wrong.
problemBody: SAT practice often ends with a score and a complete explanation. But the useful question is whether you misread the prompt, chose the wrong model, made an algebra error, or ran out of time. Lune Synth reads the attempt so the next practice block targets the cause instead of adding more random questions.
contrastAfter: Find the error pattern behind the score

benefits.title: Work it under pressure
benefits.body: Build the habit of setting up and solving SAT-style math without leaning on answer generation.

benefits.title: Diagnose the miss
benefits.body: Separate concept gaps from rushed arithmetic, misreads, and incomplete reasoning.

benefits.title: Target the next set
benefits.body: Spend limited prep time on the patterns most likely to improve your next attempt.

exampleHeadline: Turn one missed question into useful prep.
attempt: The equation is set up correctly, but both sides are not divided by the same coefficient.
observation: Your translation from words to algebra works. The isolation step is where the answer changes.
hint: Undo the multiplication before applying the constant term, then check by substitution.
nextPractice: Next mission: three linear-equation questions with increasing time pressure.
closingHeadline: Practice the reasoning you need on test day.
closingBody: Join the beta for SAT preparation built around visible work, precise corrections, and deliberate practice—not endless answer review.

headline: Build ACT speed without skipping the reasoning.
heroBody: Practice on paper, discover whether a miss came from the concept or the clock, and strengthen the exact skill before moving on.
phoneAlt: Lune Synth displaying an ACT algebra word problem
problemHeadline: Rushing through more questions does not fix a weak method.
problemBody: ACT pacing matters, but speed built on shaky reasoning collapses under pressure. Lune Synth examines the work behind each answer so you can tell a slow method from a missing concept, repair it, and then practice using it more efficiently.
contrastBefore: Chase the timer and repeat the same miss
contrastAfter: Fix the method, then build the speed

benefits.title: Make a real attempt
benefits.body: Work through ACT-style algebra and geometry with the same decisions you will make on test day.

benefits.title: Separate skill from pace
benefits.body: Identify whether the issue is setup, calculation, interpretation, or time management.

benefits.title: Practice efficiently
benefits.body: Use short targeted missions to reinforce the method before adding more time pressure.

exampleHeadline: Know why the clock beat you.
attempt: The rectangle relationship is correct, but trial-and-error replaces a faster quadratic setup.
observation: Your interpretation is accurate. The method will cost too much time across a full section.
hint: Write width as x and length as x + 7. Which equation represents the area?
nextPractice: Next mission: two area word problems using algebraic setup before calculation.

metaTitle: Help Your Child Get Unstuck in Math | Lune Synth
metaDescription: Lune Synth helps children show their math work, find the step that is breaking down, and rebuild confidence without simply giving them answers.
headline: Help your child get unstuck without giving them the answer.
heroBody: Lune Synth reads handwritten math, finds the exact step that broke down, and gives your child a manageable next move—so homework can build independence instead of conflict.
phoneAlt: Lune Synth results screen showing a grade and specific feedback on a calculus attempt
problemKicker: When ‘I don't get it’ is all you hear
problemHeadline: A child can struggle with one step and start believing they are bad at math.
problemBody: The hard part is often locating the gap. A final answer cannot show whether your child misunderstood the idea, lost a sign, or simply rushed. Lune Synth starts with the page they wrote, preserves what they did correctly, and narrows the problem to something they can actually repair.
contrastBefore: Turn homework into an answer hunt
contrastAfter: Turn one confusing step into a small win

benefits.title: See the real attempt
benefits.body: Handwritten work makes your child's reasoning visible instead of reducing learning to a final answer.

benefits.title: Protect their confidence
benefits.body: Feedback keeps the correct parts intact and focuses attention on one manageable correction.

benefits.title: Build independence
benefits.body: Targeted hints help your child continue the work without requiring you to reteach every lesson.

exampleHeadline: A better answer to ‘Where did I go wrong?’
attempt: The correct method appears on the page, but one negative sign changes the final result.
observation: Most of the reasoning is sound. The error begins on one line, not across the whole topic.
hint: Check what happens to the sign when this term moves across the equals sign.
nextPractice: Next mission: a short confidence-building set focused only on signed equations.
closingHeadline: Give their effort somewhere useful to go.
closingBody: Join the beta for early family access to math support designed to strengthen confidence, visible reasoning, and independent problem solving.
